I wanted to like this record more than I do. The first single is a legitimate gut punch — that bass tone sounds like it was recorded inside a refrigerator, in a good way — and the drumming throughout is the best work of her career. But the middle third sags in a way the sequencing can't hide. Three songs in a row sit at the same tempo, in the same key area, with the same washed-out vocal treatment, and by the time "Dovecote" arrives with actual air in it you've forgotten the album can breathe.

The lyrics are a separate problem. When she's specific, she's devastating: the line about returning the library books of a dead friend is the kind of detail you can't fake. But too often she reaches for the big abstraction instead, and the songs turn into greeting cards for grief. You can hear the better album buried in this one. Pull tracks two, seven, and nine, and you'd have an EP people would still be talking about in a decade. As it stands, it's a B-minus from an A-list talent, and the frustrating kind of B-minus, the one that comes from caution rather than ambition.
